title: ChatGPT vs Claude for writing and editing
intro: Writing quality is subjective, so the useful question is: which one needs less editing from you, on your kind of writing? Run this test with your own draft and score it.
task: Edit a rough 150-word draft into a clear version without changing the facts.
sample: Hi team, just wanted to say that the thing we talked about last week is kind of running late and we might not hit the date, because a few things came up with the supplier, so can everyone maybe think about what we can cut or move so that we do not miss the launch completely?
prompt: Act as a careful editor. Rewrite the text below so it is clear and about 70 words, for a team of colleagues. Keep my meaning. Do not add facts. After the rewrite, list the three biggest changes you made.
criteria: Matched the tone I asked for
verify: Which plan or model you are using in each tool (they differ by plan and change over time)
Limits on message length and uploads for your plan
How each handles your data: training use, retention and deletion settings

title: ChatGPT vs Claude for research and summarising
intro: For research, accuracy and traceability matter more than polish. Test both on a document you know well so you can tell what they got wrong.
task: Summarise a document and quote the sentence behind each key point.
sample: Use any public article or report you know well (500 to 1,500 words) so that you can verify the summary yourself.
prompt: Summarise the document below in: (1) a three-sentence overview, (2) five key points, (3) what is unclear or missing. Quote the exact sentence for each key point so I can check it.
criteria: Quotes really exist in the source
verify: Whether each tool can read your file type and size on your plan
Whether web search or browsing is on, and whether sources are shown

title: ChatGPT vs Claude for coding help
intro: Judge on whether the code runs and whether the explanation lets you trust it. Always run it yourself in a safe environment.
task: Find and fix a small bug and explain the cause.
prompt: This Python function crashes on an empty list. Explain why in two sentences, then give a fixed version that returns None for an empty list, and add two tests. Do not change anything else.
verify: Which models and coding tools are available on your plan
Limits on file uploads and context size
Whether code you paste is used for training under your settings
